title: v93: the sole v92 interior-gradient excess is strongly localized but not located by the preregistered initial-normal saliency

scope.dataset_role: already-open post-open BLASTNet Case 6 mechanism diagnostic

scale_localization.interpretation: The excess is primarily low-frequency and one-sided along z, not a diffuse high-frequency texture defect.

anchor_gradient_energy.post_result_role: future hypothesis generator only; it cannot replace the failed primary v93 locator

independent_validation.independent_gradient_implementation: manual second-order finite differences rather than the formal numpy.gradient helper

interpretation.what_changed: v92 left one interior-gradient failure. v93 decomposed that exact candidate-minus-ZeroK2 error without optimizing a new field and found a compact, low-frequency, z-sided defect.
interpretation.why_the_route_did_not_advance_directly: The frozen deployment-visible initial-normal saliency failed all three locator predicates, so the protocol forbids immediately building or training a local two-scale predictor.
interpretation.next_scientific_gate: Freeze a separate observable-shell diagnostic. A predeclared anchor-gradient control may generate that hypothesis, but it must earn support on local maps not used to select it or under an explicitly costed extra-call shell.
interpretation.claim_boundary: The saliency does not read the current Case6 target truth, but it inherits a frozen Case3-supervised upstream model and shared pre-v93 physics/data-loading kernels. This is a post-open localization and route-selection result, not a new reconstruction algorithm, a capacity witness, a trained operator, an external result, a speed result, real BOST, or a publication breakthrough.
